01_configurations.title: Table 1 Experimental configurations
01_configurations.caption: The two action factors define four configurations. All configurations generate shared evolution decisions; the gates determine which resulting memory changes are applied.
01_configurations.interpretation: The design isolates strengthening and neighbour evolution and their combination.
01_configurations.limitation: One stochastic memory build was accepted per conversation and configuration.

02_overall_results.title: Table 2 Evaluation across 558 matched questions
02_overall_results.caption: Question-weighted F1 and BLEU-1 percentages under the authors' historical policy and the additional alternative-reference policy. Binary adversarial correctness covers 121 questions.
02_overall_results.interpretation: Historical scoring ranks Full A-MEM highest; alternative-reference scoring ranks Neither highest.
02_overall_results.limitation: The policies differ in adversarial references. Neither policy is presented as universally superior.

03_factorial_contrasts.title: Table 3 Alternative-reference factorial contrasts
03_factorial_contrasts.caption: Matched question differences, averaged over 558 questions, in percentage points. Interaction = Full − Linking Only − Evolution Only + Neither.
03_factorial_contrasts.interpretation: The pooled interaction is positive, while the individual aggregate contrasts vary in direction.
03_factorial_contrasts.limitation: These are descriptive contrasts from single builds, without statistical significance claims.

04_category_performance.title: Table 4 Alternative-reference category performance
04_category_performance.caption: Separate F1 and BLEU-1 percentage panels show all four configurations and the five original category populations.
04_category_performance.interpretation: Linking Only has the highest multi-hop F1, while Neither has the highest pooled alternative-reference F1.
04_category_performance.limitation: Categories differ in size and difficulty; open-domain contains only 27 questions.

05_cost_retrieval.title: Table 5 Scientific inference cost and retrieval
05_cost_retrieval.caption: Mean retrieved entries per question, total native answer input tokens and identified model costs for the three accepted builds per configuration, covering 558 questions. Fees and historical attempts are excluded.
05_cost_retrieval.interpretation: Linking approximately doubles answer input tokens. Neither has the highest aggregate alternative F1 at the lowest identified model cost in this population.
05_cost_retrieval.limitation: Observed inference costs apply to this model, population and retrieval configuration.

06_conversation_results.title: Table 6 Alternative-reference results by conversation
06_conversation_results.caption: F1 and BLEU-1 percentages for all four conditions on conv-44, conv-49 and conv-50. Each question has equal weight within a conversation.
06_conversation_results.interpretation: Linking Only exceeds Neither on conv-49 and scores lower on the other two conversations.
06_conversation_results.limitation: Three conversations and one build per cell do not establish run-to-run variability.

01_scoring_comparison.title: Figure 1 Evaluation reference changes configuration ranking
01_scoring_comparison.caption: Historical and alternative-reference F1 for 558 matched questions per configuration, using a zero-based bar axis.
01_scoring_comparison.interpretation: Full A-MEM ranks highest historically and Neither ranks highest with the alternative reference.
01_scoring_comparison.limitation: Both policies score the same predictions; the alternative reference is an additional evaluation perspective.

02_category_heatmap.title: Figure 2 Alternative-reference F1 by category
02_category_heatmap.caption: Each cell gives F1 (%) to two decimals on a shared 0–100 sequential scale. Row labels include category sample sizes.
02_category_heatmap.interpretation: Linking Only leads multi-hop F1, although its aggregate F1 is below Neither.
02_category_heatmap.limitation: Small numerical differences and uneven category sizes warrant caution; no significance is implied.

03_f1_vs_cost.title: Figure 3 Alternative-reference F1 and scientific model cost
03_f1_vs_cost.caption: Each point represents three accepted scientific builds and 558 matched questions. Circles indicate the observed Pareto frontier and crosses indicate dominated configurations.
03_f1_vs_cost.interpretation: Neither strictly Pareto-dominates the other configurations on aggregate alternative F1 and identified model cost within this population.
03_f1_vs_cost.limitation: Costs exclude failed historical attempts and observability fees; this frontier is specific to the observed experiment.

04_factorial_interaction.title: Figure 4 Interaction between linking and evolution
04_factorial_interaction.caption: Alternative-reference F1 (%) with linking OFF and ON, at both evolution settings. The four-term interaction is +2.72 percentage points, indicating that evolution's effect differs according to linking status.
04_factorial_interaction.interpretation: Evolution's F1 contrast is less negative when linking is enabled. Full A-MEM does not have the highest pooled F1.
04_factorial_interaction.limitation: The pooled interaction varies by conversation and is descriptive. The line axis is zoomed; endpoint values are shown.

05_token_overhead.title: Figure 5 Retrieval expansion and token overhead
05_token_overhead.caption: Separate zero-based panels show native answer input tokens in millions and mean retrieved entries per question for 558 questions per configuration.
05_token_overhead.interpretation: Linking-expanded retrieval approximately doubles the answer input token volume.
05_token_overhead.limitation: Token volume measures input overhead, not answer quality or a universal efficiency effect.

06_dual_scoring_f1_vs_cost.title: Figure 6 Cost–performance trade-offs under two evaluation policies
06_dual_scoring_f1_vs_cost.caption: Historical (A) and alternative-reference (B) F1 use identical costs and shared numerical scales for 558 matched questions per configuration and three accepted scientific builds each. Filled points indicate Pareto efficiency; hollow points indicate domination. The dotted line connects the three historical frontier points. Costs include only identified scientific model inference charges.
06_dual_scoring_f1_vs_cost.interpretation: Neither, Linking Only and Full A-MEM form the observed historical frontier. Neither alone forms the alternative-reference frontier. Answer-quality references therefore change the cost–performance interpretation.
06_dual_scoring_f1_vs_cost.limitation: These are descriptive comparisons within the measured population, with one build per conversation and configuration. No statistical significance or universal efficiency is implied.

07_dual_policy_category_heatmap.title: Figure 7 Category F1 under historical and complementary references
07_dual_policy_category_heatmap.caption: Each panel shows five question categories across the four configurations. Parentheses give the number of matched questions. Both panels use the same 0–100% F1 scale.
07_dual_policy_category_heatmap.interpretation: Only adversarial references change. Full leads adversarial F1 under the historical reference, while Neither leads under the complementary reference.
07_dual_policy_category_heatmap.limitation: Each conversation and configuration contributes one stochastic build.
